title: Support Operations Analysis Report
executive_summary: Analysis of 347 support tickets reveals a total labor cost of $27,422.90 and a mean resolution time of 75.2 minutes. Team Beta carries the highest labor spend, phone is the fastest channel, and email tickets reopen at roughly twice the rate of chat tickets. A small high-cost, low-satisfaction segment (12 tickets) warrants targeted intervention. Agent workload is moderately concentrated, with the busiest agent handling 7.5% of all tickets.

key_findings.statement: The dataset contains 347 tickets with a mean resolution time of 75.2 minutes and a total labor cost of $27,422.90.
Team Beta incurred the highest labor cost at $10,247.36, followed by Gamma at $9,387.73 and Alpha at $7,787.81. Beta's spend exceeds Alpha's by $2,459.55.
Phone is the fastest channel at 69.3 minutes mean resolution, followed by email at 73.0 minutes and chat at 83.0 minutes.
Email tickets reopen at 17.2% versus 7.8% for chat, representing an increase of approximately 119.8% relative to the chat reopen rate.
Twelve tickets meet the high-cost (labor_cost ≥ $100) and low-satisfaction (score ≤ 2) criteria, with a reopen rate of 8.3% — a segment that merits priority review.

Resolution time has a median of 65.0 minutes and a standard deviation of 51.9 minutes, indicating a right-skewed distribution. Mean satisfaction (where recorded) is 4.15 out of 5, with 19 tickets missing a satisfaction score.
Eighteen distinct agents handled the 347 tickets. The busiest single agent resolved 26 tickets, representing 7.5% of total volume — a moderate but notable concentration.

limitations: Nineteen tickets (5.5%) are missing satisfaction scores, which may introduce bias into the satisfaction mean and the high-cost low-satisfaction segment count.
Labor cost is derived from the export and may not capture indirect costs such as escalation overhead or managerial review time.
The dataset represents a single export snapshot; seasonal or trend effects cannot be assessed without time-series data.
Agent identity is based on agent_id from the roster join; any mismatches or unmatched records during cleaning could affect agent concentration metrics.
Reopen rates are based on a binary reopened flag and do not capture multiple reopenings or partial resolutions.
conclusion: Support operations are broadly healthy, with a mean satisfaction of 4.15 and a median resolution of 65 minutes. However, three areas warrant action: (1) Team Beta's labor cost is 31.6% above Alpha's and should be reviewed for efficiency; (2) email's reopen rate is ~120% higher than chat's, suggesting process or quality gaps in email handling; and (3) the 12 high-cost, low-satisfaction tickets represent a concentrated risk that should be audited individually.
